selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What warning is given at the beginning about people who feel happy about what they arranged and want praise for things they did not do?
questions.answer: They should not think they are safe from punishment, because painful punishment awaits them.

questions.question: Which part of a person is especially being corrected here?
questions.answer: The commanding self that pushes toward wrong desires.

questions.question: What mistake would the self make if it copied the seed or branch in the wrong way?
questions.answer: It would think it deserves all the credit for what appears through it.

questions.question: What does pride do to the blessings a person has?
questions.answer: It reduces their worth.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of thanklessness?
questions.answer: It cancels blessings.

questions.question: What should replace showing off good deeds?
questions.answer: Thanking Allah.

questions.question: What is the similarity between the human self and nature in the world?
questions.answer: Both receive good and are places where evil is linked, rather than being the true source of good.

questions.question: How can the self become connected to evil?
questions.answer: By failing to welcome good as it should.

questions.question: Why should the self not say, “I was the place where beauty showed up, so I deserve beauty”?
questions.answer: Because beauty passing through something does not prove that thing owns or absorbs it.

questions.question: What reason is given for being chosen to receive gifts first?
questions.answer: Greater need and poverty, not greater greatness.

questions.question: What kind of people are warned of painful suffering in the opening verse?
questions.answer: People who delight in what they managed and want credit for things they never did.

questions.question: What kind of self is being warned and corrected?
questions.answer: A proud self that loves status and praise.

questions.question: Why is the self said to deserve blame again and again?
questions.answer: Because it acts proudly even though it should be thankful and humble.

questions.question: What is one harmful result of pride?
questions.answer: It lowers the worth of blessings.

questions.question: What does the passage say ingratitude does to blessings?
questions.answer: It erases their value.

questions.question: Instead of wanting praise, what should a person seek?
questions.answer: Repentance and asking Allah for forgiveness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes a person truly complete?
questions.answer: Realizing Allah and not living around the ego.

questions.question: Why are hiddenly ugly things linked to self and nature?
questions.answer: So Allah’s purity from faults is understood.

questions.question: What big mistake does a person make by worshipping nature or the self?
questions.answer: The person gives created things a place that belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: What answer is given to someone who says, “Beautiful works appeared through me, so I must have merit”?
questions.answer: The gifts came not because of merit, but because of greater need and poverty.

questions.question: What false hope is denied in the verse at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The hope of escaping punishment while loving undeserved praise.

questions.question: What do the fruit examples teach about where success comes from?
questions.answer: Success and blessings come from a true giver, not from the object that merely carries them.

questions.question: What lesson should the self learn from those examples?
questions.answer: It should not become proud over blessings shown through it.

questions.question: Why is the self especially responsible for its mistakes?
questions.answer: Because it has the ability to choose.

title: Title and 1 Point Discipline and Gratitude Lesson for the Commanding Self
